description: A team capstone in which students take an embedded, robotic or communications system from client need to a demonstrated prototype. They draw the architecture, build and wire the hardware and firmware in the lab, plan and test the system, and defend their decisions in design reviews.
modelledOn: Barr and Massa, Programming Embedded Systems
ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288, Systems and software engineering: System life cycle processes
Project Management Institute, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge
outcomes: Convert a stakeholder need into measurable requirements, a feasibility case and a project proposal.
Decompose a system into hardware, firmware and software blocks and specify every interface between them.
Build, wire and integrate a working prototype in stages, debugging faults with measurement tools.
Plan and execute verification against traceable requirements and report results with stated uncertainty.
Plan and track a project with a work breakdown structure, Gantt chart, critical path, budget and risk register.
Present and defend design decisions, safety and ethical judgements in a review and a final demonstration.

units.title: Project proposal and requirements
topics: Choosing a problem: stakeholder interviews and needs analysis (cold-chain monitoring, solar pumping, rural connectivity, farm robotics)
Requirements: functional and non-functional, MoSCoW priority and a traceability matrix
Feasibility: technical, economic and schedule checks and a first risk register
Prior-art and standards search: what exists, what can be reused, what must be respected
Writing the proposal: problem statement, objectives, deliverables and success criteria

units.title: System architecture and interface specification
topics: Functional decomposition and block diagrams across hardware, firmware and software
Hardware and software partitioning: choosing a microcontroller or single-board computer, sensors, actuators and radios
Interface specification: signal levels, pin maps and protocols (UART, SPI, I2C, CAN, MQTT) and data formats
Power budget, timing budget and memory budget
Interface control documents and change control
Architecture trade study with a weighted decision matrix

units.title: Hardware design and prototyping
topics: Schematic capture, component selection and the bill of materials
Breadboard to perfboard to PCB: grounding, decoupling, layout and electromagnetic compatibility
Sensor and actuator interfacing: ADC, PWM, H-bridges and signal conditioning
Power supplies, batteries and solar charging; protection against reverse polarity, overcurrent and surges
Enclosure and environment: heat, dust, humidity and vibration in West African conditions

units.title: Firmware and system integration
topics: Firmware architecture: super-loop, interrupt-driven design and RTOS tasks
Drivers and the hardware abstraction layer; unit-testable firmware
Communication stack: MQTT over GSM or Wi-Fi, LoRa links and over-the-air updates
Incremental integration: bottom-up builds, stubs and mocks, hardware-in-the-loop
Debugging toolkit: logic analyser, serial trace, watchdogs and fault injection

units.title: Verification and test planning
topics: Test strategy: V-model, unit, integration, system and acceptance tests
Test cases traced to requirements with pass/fail criteria
Measurement uncertainty, calibration and data logging
Reliability: burn-in, failure modes and effects analysis and mean time between failures
Planning a field trial and a data-collection protocol

units.title: Project management and Gantt planning
topics: Work breakdown structure, Gantt charts and the critical path
Agile for hardware: sprints, milestones and prototype iterations
Budget, procurement lead times and supply-chain risk
Team roles, version control, issue tracking and documentation habits
Risk monitoring, earned value and re-planning after a slip

units.title: Design review, safety and ethics
topics: Preliminary and critical design reviews: what evidence a panel expects
Safety: electrical, battery, mechanical and radio-frequency exposure; applying standards
Professional ethics and codes of conduct; engineering responsibility when a design fails
Environmental impact, e-waste and sustainability
Regulation and licensing: spectrum, type approval and data protection
Intellectual property and open hardware and software licences

units.title: Final demonstration and report
topics: Demonstration plan, script and rehearsal with a fallback
Technical report structure, figures, tables and references
Poster and oral presentation for technical and non-technical audiences
Evaluation against requirements, lessons learned and future work
Handover package: user manual, maintenance guide and source repository

schedule.title: Finding the problem
schedule.exercise: Interview a (role-played) clinic manager or farmer about a monitoring problem, then write ten requirements, classify them functional or non-functional and rank them with MoSCoW.

tasks.title: Run a stakeholder interview scenario for a vaccine cold-chain problem, choose the questions that expose real needs, and score the notes gathered
Build a requirements traceability table for ten requirements linking each to a stakeholder need and a planned verification method
Resolve a scenario where two stakeholders give conflicting requirements for a solar pump controller and justify your prioritisation against a rubric

schedule.title: Feasibility and the proposal
schedule.exercise: Write a three-page proposal with a problem statement, objectives, deliverables, success criteria, a literature and standards list, a feasibility argument and a risk register of eight risks.

tasks.title: Create a risk register for a capstone with eight risks scored by likelihood and impact, each with an owner and a mitigation
Review a prior-art scenario with three existing products and decide what to reuse, what to build and what standard constrains the design
Critique a flawed project proposal against a rubric covering objectives, measurable success criteria and feasibility, and rewrite its weakest section

schedule.title: From needs to architecture
schedule.exercise: Draw a block diagram for your project that splits the system into hardware, firmware and software blocks, assign a microcontroller and write the interface table for every connection.

tasks.title: Draw a block diagram of a soil-moisture irrigation controller with sensor, controller, valve driver, radio and power blocks, labelling every signal between them
Wire an Arduino to an I2C temperature sensor and an SPI display, record the pin map and verify readings against the written interface table
Choose between an AVR board and a Raspberry Pi for a camera-based counter, justify with pin, speed, power and cost data, and prototype the choice

schedule.title: Budgets, interfaces and trade studies
schedule.exercise: Produce a power budget and timing budget for the design, an interface control document with version numbers, and a weighted decision matrix for one major component choice.

tasks.title: Measure the current draw of a sensor node in active and sleep states and compute battery life for a 2000 mAh cell
Write an interface control document entry for an MQTT topic tree including payload fields, units, rates and a version number
Score three radio options (GSM, LoRa, Wi-Fi) for a rural monitoring site in a trade-study scenario and defend the weighted decision before a panel

schedule.title: Schematics, parts and prototypes
schedule.exercise: Capture a schematic for the sensor and driver stage, produce a bill of materials with two suppliers per part and build the stage on a breadboard, then compare the measurement with the design values.

tasks.title: Draw a schematic block with a sensor, op-amp stage and ADC input, and generate a bill of materials with part numbers, quantities and unit costs
Drive a DC motor through an H-bridge with PWM from an Arduino and measure speed against duty cycle at five settings
Diagnose a noisy analogue sensor reading in a prototype, apply decoupling and a filter, and show with logged samples that noise is reduced

schedule.title: Power, protection and the physical product
schedule.exercise: Design a solar and battery supply for a field node: size the panel and battery for three cloudy days, add reverse-polarity and overcurrent protection and sketch an enclosure for dust and humidity.

tasks.title: Size a solar panel and battery for a node drawing 120 mA average, check the daily energy balance and test a regulator under load
Add a fuse and a reverse-polarity diode to a power rail, then inject a fault and verify the protection limits current as designed
Work through an environment scenario of a failed unit returned from a humid site, choose the root cause from evidence and specify a design change

schedule.title: Firmware architecture and drivers
schedule.exercise: Structure the firmware as drivers, a hardware abstraction layer and an application layer, and write a telemetry loop that publishes sensor readings over MQTT.

tasks.title: Convert a blocking super-loop sensor program to an interrupt-driven design that samples at 10 Hz, and verify the timing on the serial trace
Write a sensor driver behind a small interface, then swap in a mock driver so the application logic runs without hardware
Publish temperature readings from a Raspberry Pi to an MQTT broker with a retained status message and a last-will message, and check delivery

schedule.title: Integration and debugging
schedule.exercise: Integrate sensors, actuator and communications in three increments, logging what broke at each step, and fix one injected fault using a logic analyser or serial trace.

tasks.title: Integrate a sensor, a relay and an MQTT link in stages, with a passing check recorded after each stage
Find an intentionally wrong I2C address and a swapped SPI clock phase in a given sketch using the trace view and fix both
Use a terminal on a Linux gateway to read the serial log, filter the faulty messages and add a watchdog that restarts the service on failure

schedule.title: Verification and test planning
schedule.exercise: Write a test plan with at least fifteen test cases traced to requirements, include calibration and uncertainty for one measurement, and plan a failure modes and effects analysis for the five riskiest parts.

tasks.title: Build a test matrix of ten test cases that each trace to a requirement, with inputs, expected results and pass/fail criteria
Calibrate a temperature sensor against two reference points, fit the correction, and state the measurement uncertainty from ten repeated readings
Perform a failure modes and effects analysis in a scenario for a battery-powered sensor, ranking failures by risk priority and proposing controls

schedule.title: Planning, scheduling and risk
schedule.exercise: Build a work breakdown structure and a Gantt chart for the remaining weeks, mark the critical path, set a budget with lead times and reschedule after a two-week part delay.

tasks.title: Draw a Gantt chart from a work breakdown structure of 15 tasks with dependencies and highlight the critical path and total float
Re-plan a project after a component with a three-week lead time arrives late and report the new finish date and the tasks that moved
Handle a management scenario with budget overrun and a team member leaving, choosing re-planning options and scoring against a rubric

schedule.title: Design reviews, safety and ethics
schedule.exercise: Hold a mock critical design review: present the design, evidence and open risks to a panel, then write a safety and ethics statement covering batteries, radio exposure, e-waste and licensing.

tasks.title: Present a design review scenario, choose the evidence that answers the panel's five questions and decide whether to proceed to build
Assess the safety case for a lithium battery pack in a scenario and select protections required by the relevant standard
Resolve an ethics case in which a client asks to hide a known calibration defect, scoring each decision against a professional code

schedule.title: Demonstration and report
schedule.exercise: Rehearse the final demonstration with a fallback plan, draft the report outline with figures and tables, and prepare a one-page poster for a non-technical audience.

tasks.title: Run the demonstration script end to end on the prototype three times, record failures and add a recovery step for each
Produce the system architecture figure and the Gantt summary figure for the report with consistent labels and captions
Deliver an oral presentation scenario to a mixed panel and choose how to explain a failed test honestly, scored on clarity and candour

schedule.title: Evaluation and handover
schedule.exercise: Evaluate the prototype against every requirement in a results table, write lessons learned and future work, and assemble the handover package with a user manual and repository.

tasks.title: Fill in a requirements compliance table marking each requirement met, partly met or not met with the evidence reference
Run a retrospective scenario, sort what went well and what failed, and propose three changes ranked by effect on the next team
Prepare a handover repository with a README, a tagged release and a clear build and flash procedure, and test it on a clean machine
